detailed_rationale:
Tanla is a CPaaS/enterprise-messaging business (A2P SMS, Trubloq blockchain-based scam-blocking, and the newer Wisely AI fraud-protection platform) whose moat is largely regulatory: it is a key infrastructure partner in India's DLT/anti-spam telecom framework, which gives it a durable position in domestic A2P messaging even as per-message pricing keeps drifting down. FY26 revenue reached a record Rs 4,418 cr (+9.7% YoY), but full-year PAT growth was close to flat (~+0.4%, per Whalesbook's FY26 recap) despite gross profit growing 11.8% -- meaning opex/investment (platform build-out, Wisely AI scale-up) absorbed most of the operating gains for three quarters of the year.

Q4 FY26 was a distinct improvement on that full-year picture: revenue +15% YoY to Rs 1,178 cr, PAT +14.5% YoY to Rs 134 cr, and the highest-ever quarterly gross profit (Rs 317.8 cr, +22.8% YoY) -- so the exit rate is meaningfully better than the FY26 average, consistent with Wisely AI monetisation (it protected 100 million Indosat users from 2bn+ scam/spam attempts within six months of deployment) starting to scale internationally rather than being a pure domestic cost centre.

The balance sheet is close to debt-free (D/E 0.02, interest cover >100x) and returns are high (ROE 25%, ROCE 33%), yet the stock trades at only ~15x earnings -- a discount to what a 25% ROE, net-cash compounder would typically command. That gap reflects real concerns: revenue CAGR has been mid-to-high single digits for three years (9.6%), domestic A2P SMS is a mature, price-competitive, regulation-dependent market, and Wisely AI's international scale-up is unproven as a P&L driver beyond pilot deployments. The cheap multiple is compensation for growth-durability risk, not obviously a mispricing.
recommendation_rationale: Quant call is already Hold; the low leverage and high returns do not, on their own, justify treating this as a rescue candidate (it was never a quant-Sell) and the flat full-year PAT growth against a backdrop of a mature core market argues against a more constructive stance than Hold.
summary: Tanla is a profitable, debt-free messaging-infrastructure business trading at a below-market multiple (~15x earnings) for its return profile (25% ROE). Full-year profit growth was close to flat despite double-digit revenue growth, though the most recent quarter showed a clear improvement as its newer Wisely AI fraud-protection platform scales. We rate this a Hold: the balance sheet and returns are excellent, but revenue growth has been modest and the path to reaccelerating it depends on unproven new-platform monetisation.
positive_para: Net-cash balance sheet (D/E 0.02, interest cover >100x), 25% ROE / 33% ROCE, and a regulatory moat in India's anti-spam/DLT messaging infrastructure. Q4 FY26 showed real acceleration -- revenue +15% YoY, gross profit +22.8% YoY, the highest quarterly gross profit on record -- and Wisely AI is already protecting tens of millions of users at an international telco (Indosat), suggesting a second growth leg beyond domestic A2P SMS. Trades at ~15x earnings, cheap for the quality of the balance sheet.
negative_para: Three-year revenue CAGR of just 9.6% and a full FY26 PAT growth of roughly flat (~+0.4%) despite a double-digit revenue increase show that opex/investment intensity is currently absorbing most operating gains -- the Q4 improvement needs to be sustained, not a one-quarter blip, before the growth story re-rates. Domestic A2P SMS pricing is structurally declining, and Wisely AI's revenue contribution outside pilot deployments is not yet demonstrated at scale.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~15x earnings for a 25% ROE, net-cash business, the market is pricing low-single-digit-to-flat forward growth -- essentially crediting none of the Wisely AI optionality and extrapolating the mature domestic A2P trend. If Q4's better trajectory (revenue +15%, gross profit +23%) holds for a few more quarters, the stock is cheap; if FY26's near-flat full-year PAT growth turns out to be the more representative run-rate, 15x is a fair, not a bargain, multiple. Leaning toward fair value with asymmetric upside if the Q4 trend is real.
